solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Deposit in total, what you'll cough up

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside that other word

blocks.note: a total is a sum
to deposit something is to put it down

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to cough up a deposit in full, as if paying money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cough up' suggests paying money, but it is meant literally: the answer is phlegm.
explanation.definitionFit: Sputum is the mucus and phlegm expelled from the lungs by coughing.

clue.text: Fish, a lot no decent chap's taken on board

indicators.note: taken on board ship means put between the letters standing for a steamship

blocks.note: first meaning: plural of scad, a horse mackerel
second meaning: large quantities
a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably

explanation.surface: A lot of fish, and some disreputable man has been let aboard the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: On board means inside SS, the steamship abbreviation; the answer also gets two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Scads are both fish of the horse-mackerel family and, informally, large numbers of anything.

clue.text: Irregular or GI consorting with pro, resulting in skin disease

indicators.note: irregular means out of order, so these letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An irregular soldier or GI going with a prostitute catches a skin complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consorting with' simply joins the two lots of fodder; it has a sly double meaning with pro.
explanation.definitionFit: Porrigo is an old medical name for scalp diseases such as ringworm and favus.

clue.text: Two-barrelled gun: one on redan blasted channel port

indicators.note: something blasted is blown apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

blocks.note: 'un is a dialect form of one, as in 'a good 'un'
a redan is a fortification; its letters are rearranged
Dover is the English Channel port

explanation.surface: A shotgun blasts a fortification near a Channel port.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above. A redan is a V-shaped fieldwork.
explanation.definitionFit: An under-and-over is a shotgun with its two barrels mounted one above the other.

clue.text: High water cheers sailors

blocks.note: ta is a British informal thank you, like cheers
the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Sailors cheer at high tide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High water' suggests a tide, but it is water up a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarn is a small mountain lake, so water found at height.

clue.text: Deity bishop removed from mosque niche (about time)

indicators.note: removed from tells you to take one letter out of the longer word
about means going round, so the rest wraps around the inserted letter

blocks.note: the mihrab is the niche in a mosque facing Mecca
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A bishop is ejected from a mosque niche, with a time reference in brackets.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the B from the niche and wrap the remainder round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Mithra (Mithras) is the ancient Persian god of light, worshipped in a Roman mystery cult.

clue.text: What Trump's opponents call him, crudely: 'Low, grabbing advantage' (6, two words)

definitions.text: What Trump's opponents call him, crudely

indicators.note: a word that grabs another holds it in its grip, so it surrounds it

blocks.note: a low voice or note is bass
AD is the tennis abbreviation for advantage

explanation.surface: Trump's critics call him something crude, a low man grabbing any advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: AD is short for 'advantage' in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A crude insult his critics might use: 'bad' plus 'ass', meaning a contemptible, foolish person.

clue.text: Pouch-like undergarment regularly making room for US line

indicators.note: making room at regular intervals means the letters are slotted in one at a time between letters of the garment

blocks.note: a bra is an undergarment
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: An undergarment has pockets added for an American line of goods.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes after B and S after R, so the letters alternate, then L follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Bursal describes a bursa, a fluid-filled sac or pouch in the body.

clue.text: Restrain flow of poet about love? Chequers needs one!

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word wraps around another

blocks.note: to dam a river is to hold back its flow
a bard is a poet
love is nil in tennis, like O

explanation.surface: Holding back the outpourings of a love poet, and a nod to the Prime Minister's country house.
explanation.walkthrough: Chequers is the British Prime Minister's country residence, but here it is the game of draughts (checkers).
explanation.definitionFit: A dam-board is a Scots or old word for a draughtboard, the board checkers is played on.

clue.text: Ena hesitates, quivering, ready for op?

indicators.note: quivering means shaking, and shaken letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A nervous woman called Ena hesitates, trembling before her operation.
explanation.walkthrough: Ena is a stock crossword name; the definition is a verb phrase, to make ready for surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: To anaesthetise a patient is to deaden sensation, preparing them for surgery.

clue.text: Bristles, minimum of effort having been put into food served up

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means brought upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top
something put into another goes inside it

blocks.note: eats is slang for food
the least of 'effort' is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone bristles that minimal effort went into the food served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bristles' looks like a verb of annoyance but is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Setae are stiff bristles or hairs on animals such as worms and insects.

clue.text: Bleak role in hospital

indicators.note: a word sitting in another goes inside it

blocks.note: san is short for sanatorium
a role in a play is a part

explanation.surface: Someone has a gloomy job in a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan means austere and frugal, so bleak in the sense of bare and comfortless.

clue.text: Gland that's uric an MO treated

indicators.note: something treated is processed and altered, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor treats a gland producing uric acid.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is the usual abbreviation for a medical officer, which makes the surface read medically.
explanation.definitionFit: The conarium is an old anatomical name for the pineal gland, from its cone shape.

clue.text: Tissue frameworks giving support – second's folded in layers

indicators.note: folding something over turns it back on itself, so the word is read backwards
sitting in another word means being placed inside it

blocks.note: strata are layers, as of rock
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: Some structure gives support, with a second part folded into layers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving support' completes the definition rather than starting the wordplay: stromata support tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroma is the connective framework of an organ or cell that supports its working tissue; the plural is stromata.

clue.text: Drowned of old in Dee rip

blocks.note: Dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D
a rip or tear is a rent

explanation.surface: Someone drowned long ago in a rip current on the River Dee.
explanation.walkthrough: Dee looks like the river, but it is just the name of the letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: Drent is an archaic past participle of drench, used by Spenser to mean drowned.

clue.text: End of ale in a pub put up with locally

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter only
sitting in something means being placed inside it

blocks.note: a pub is a bar
the last letter of ale

explanation.surface: The last of the ale in a local pub has to be tolerated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locally' marks a dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Abear is a dialect verb meaning to tolerate or endure, usually in 'can't abear'.

clue.text: Indian factotum, knight of the road?

blocks.note: Sir is a knight's title
a car is a vehicle of the road

explanation.surface: An Indian servant is pictured as a 'knight of the road', a tramp or travelling salesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knight of the road' is a phrase for a tramp or highwayman, but it splits into title plus a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a sircar was a house steward or general manager of a household's accounts, a factotum.

clue.text: Indicator of smoker's intake? Poisonous stuff holds it up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from the bottom, so backwards
a word that holds another has it inside

blocks.note: coniine (conine) is the poison in hemlock
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some poison holds it up, perhaps explaining a smoker's intake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poisonous stuff' suggests nicotine itself, a near-anagram of the answer, but it is hemlock's poison.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotinine is a metabolite of nicotine, measured in blood or urine to gauge tobacco exposure.

clue.text: Wader rolling eggs to mount

indicators.note: something rolling turns over, so the word comes back the other way

blocks.note: ova are eggs
to mount a jewel is to set it

explanation.surface: A wading bird rolls its eggs into place before sitting on them.
explanation.definitionFit: The avoset (usually avocet) is a long-legged wading bird with an upturned bill.

clue.text: Rat set free? That was harsh

blocks.note: a rat or scab is a strikebreaker
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A rat was released, and that was a harsh decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat' looks like the animal but is a worker who breaks a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Scabrid means rough or scurfy to the touch, so harsh in texture.

clue.text: A tidal surging round dam in Mediterranean region

indicators.note: surging water churns about, so these letters are stirred into a new order
going round something means surrounding it

blocks.note: taken as written
a dam is an animal's mother, and mother is MA

explanation.surface: A tidal surge sweeps round a dam somewhere on the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mediterranean is famously almost tideless, which adds a joke; 'dam' is a mother, not a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalmatia is the coastal region of Croatia on the Adriatic, an arm of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Snubs foreign ladies, first to last

indicators.note: moving the first letter to the last position rotates the word

blocks.note: signore is the Italian plural of signora, a lady

explanation.surface: Someone snubs some ladies from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub people is to ignore them deliberately.

clue.text: She was barefoot on screen – see stories with special appeal

blocks.note: contes are short stories, from French
SA is the usual abbreviation for sex appeal, here dressed up as special appeal

explanation.surface: A cross-reference: for the barefoot film star, see the stories with special appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Barefoot Contessa is a 1954 film starring Ava Gardner.
explanation.definitionFit: A contessa is an Italian countess, and the title role in the film The Barefoot Contessa.

clue.text: Unaccompanied men at dance with energy in legs

indicators.note: a letter sitting in another word goes inside it

blocks.note: men who go to a dance without partners go stag
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Single men at a dance show energy in their legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legs' reads as limbs, but means parts of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Stages and legs are both sections of a journey or competition.

clue.text: Jordan, say, showing line for start of effluvium, a great outpouring

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter swaps in for another
the start of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: Jordan Spieth, the American golfer, is an example of a Jordan
L is the abbreviation for line
first letter of effluvium

explanation.surface: Jordan, the country, has a great outflow of effluent along a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jordan, say' points away from the country or river to golfer Jordan Spieth; replace his E with L.
explanation.definitionFit: Spilth is an old word for something spilt, or a lavish overflow.

clue.text: Cold inside, put it on – one can't help oneself

indicators.note: one letter is put inside the rest of the wordplay

blocks.note: to put on is to add, followed by it
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone with a cold is told to wrap up inside, as if they couldn't stop themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'can't help oneself', meaning cannot resist rather than cannot assist.
explanation.definitionFit: An addict is a person compulsively dependent on something, unable to stop themselves.

clue.text: Sort of photocopy made by Cameron, old

blocks.note: Cameron Diaz, the American film actress
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An old photocopy made by David Cameron, the politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Cameron suggests the former British Prime Minister, but it is actress Cameron Diaz.
explanation.definitionFit: A diazo is a copy made by the diazotype process, the dyeline method of copying plans.

clue.text: Place including study, rarely modest

indicators.note: a word including another holds it within itself

blocks.note: to place something is to put it
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A modest place is rarely one that includes a study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' marks a rare word, part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pudent is a rare word for modest or bashful, related to pudency and impudent.

clue.text: Pastry served up with slice of tomato in ristorante

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means brought upward, so read backwards
a slice is a small piece, here a single letter, the first

blocks.note: a tart is a pastry
the first letter of tomato

explanation.surface: In an Italian restaurant, pastry is served with a slice of tomato.
explanation.definitionFit: A tratt is colloquial short for trattoria, an Italian restaurant, which is what ristorante means.

clue.text: Girl filled with love – what Cliff sought early on?

indicators.note: something filled with another thing has it inside

blocks.note: bint is slang for a girl or woman
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A girl filled with love is just what Cliff Richard was after in his early days.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff Richard's early hit 'Living Doll' was about getting a living doll; the answer means a living thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A biont is a living organism, so Cliff's living doll could jokingly be called one.

clue.text: Company member? One program for training officers backed

indicators.note: backed means put into reverse, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a means one
the Reserve Officers' Training Corps, a US college program

explanation.surface: A member of a firm signs up for an officer training program.
explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling 'program' hints at the US Reserve Officers' Training Corps. 'Company' is a theatre company, not a business.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor belongs to a theatrical company, so is a company member in that sense.

clue.text: Tin containing a bit of yellow or blue- green

indicators.note: a bit of a word is just one letter of it, the first
a word containing another has it inside

blocks.note: a tin is a can
the first letter of yellow

explanation.surface: A tin holding some yellow paint, or else blue-green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' links wordplay and definition, though it reads as a choice of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyan is a greenish-blue colour, one of the printing primaries.

clue.text: Navy girl going out in crazy fashion

indicators.note: a girl going out on the town is wild and disordered, so these letters are scattered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor girl on a night out behaves wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravingly means madly or wildly, as in raving mad.

clue.text: Scots advance in Latvian system for transferring alphabets

indicators.note: the first piece is placed in the word that follows it

blocks.note: a Lett is a Latvian
rase is a Scots form of rise, an advance or increase

explanation.surface: A Scottish advance comes within a Latvian system.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lett is a native of Latvia.
explanation.definitionFit: Letraset is a trade name for dry-transfer lettering: sheets of letters rubbed onto paper.

clue.text: Mimic female birds or sea fish

blocks.note: to do someone is to impersonate them
a ree is a female ruff, also called a reeve

explanation.surface: Someone can imitate either female birds or fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' joins the halves and is easily read as offering a choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A doree is the John Dory, a flat-bodied sea fish; the plural is dorees.

clue.text: Just about in command, though old

indicators.note: one word sitting in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: hest is an archaic word for a command, as in behest; 'though old' marks it as obsolete
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is in command, though old, and only just.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'barely' but means fair; 'old' tells you the command word is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and honest both describe a person who is fair and upright.
